reuse.why: Five server copies of the midpoint rule are routed to the existing shared getScheduledAmount, but the new API expectedAmount field re-implements the rule inline instead of calling that helper.

duplication.why: The inline ternary chain in scheduleModel.toExternal duplicates the missing/number/range dispatch of getScheduledAmount and has drifted from it (still furthest-from-zero, no approximate handling).

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts where the tree keeps schedule amount logic; only the API model computes its own copy in the API mapping layer.

scope.why: Edits are tied to the requested rule changes and the new field; the Omit<'expectedAmount'> type adjustments on create/update are necessary consequences rather than unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: Most consumers now share one definition, but the API field silently diverges from it and desktop-client callers do not pass the op, so the approximate rule is applied inconsistently; the positional false for inverse at every new call is awkward.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal computes expectedAmount inline instead of calling getScheduledAmount(schedule._amount, false, schedule._amountOp).

disguised_duplication.where: api-models.ts expectedAmount: the missing/number/range dispatch of getScheduledAmount reshaped as a nested ternary with an abs comparison, now out of sync with the shared rule.

abstraction_drift.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount gains an optional op parameter and an isapprox branch; api-models.ts toExternal bypasses it (desktop-client callers also call it without op).
